identity.name: Ransomware Precursor Auto-Containment — BlackSuit DCSync-to-ESXi Kill Chain Fires XSOAR Auto-Containment (T1003.006 / T1053.005 / T1486)
identity.summary: Ignoble Scorpius (BlackSuit) chains a vished VPN credential into DCSync on a domain controller and AnyDesk/RAT scheduled-task persistence. A correlation stitches that junction into ONE incident and fires an XSOAR R&R playbook (isolate DC, disable the stolen account, block egress) so the T1486 ESXi mass-encryption is contained, not observed. Measures MTTC/automation-rate, not just MTTD.
identity.description: Anatomy of a BlackSuit ransomware blitz attributed to Ignoble Scorpius (Unit 42): the operator vished an employee into surrendering a legitimate VPN credential (T1078), used that foothold to run a DCSync/DRSUAPI DsGetNCChanges replication request from a non-domain-controller context against a domain controller and extract NTDS.dit hashes including a highly-privileged service account (T1003.006), then registered AnyDesk plus a custom RAT as a scheduled-task persistence mechanism on the DC to survive reboots (T1053.005). From there the actor mapped the estate with Advanced IP Scanner and moved laterally over RDP and SMBExec (T1021.001 / T1570), staged and exfiltrated over 400GB with a renamed rclone binary (T1020), ran CCleaner to wipe forensic evidence (T1070), and finally pushed the BlackSuit encryptor to hundreds of VMs across ~60 VMware ESXi hosts via an Ansible playbook, encrypting them simultaneously (T1486). This card is an ANALYTICS / F5 (Automation & Workflow) scenario: its whole thesis is that Cortex XSIAM should stitch the early DCSync + DC-persistence signals into a single 'Ransomware Precursor' incident and auto-fire an XSOAR Response & Remediation playbook AT THE JUNCTION — isolate the domain controller, disable the stolen service account, block the exfil egress ASN — so the encryption impact is pre-empted. The primary KPI is not detection latency (MTTD) but Mean-Time-To-Contain / automation-rate: the correlation must fire AND the playbook must complete before T1486 detonates. Three BIOCs cover the VPN valid-account anomaly, the DCSync-from-non-DC replication, and the DC scheduled-task persistence; one endpoint ABIOC fuses the DCSync->persistence behavioral chain on the DC; supporting validation XQL confirms the lateral movement and the renamed-rclone bulk egress; and the terminal correlation rule CR-MP-0020 raises the single precursor incident and triggers the auto-containment playbook, with a metric XQL asserting the playbook fired and closed the incident before impact.

campaigns: BlackSuit ransomware blitz — DCSync-to-ESXi mass-encryption intrusions (2024-2026)

data_sources: Active Directory: Active Directory Object Access

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-MP-020 — BlackSuit DCSync-to-ESXi precursor auto-containment; correlation-terminal F5 automation scenario driven by the CortexSim orchestrator (non-destructive echo simulation of the kill-chain junctions).

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM agents on the domain controllers and member hosts so DCSync replication, scheduled-task persistence, and lateral-movement process lineage reach xdr_data / msft_windows_security.
prerequisites.check_command: systemctl status cortex-agent || sc query cyserver

prerequisites.description: An XSOAR Response & Remediation playbook is wired to the 'Ransomware Precursor' correlation so the DCSync+persistence junction can auto-isolate the DC, disable the stolen account, and block egress.
prerequisites.check_command: echo 'confirm XSOAR playbook Ransomware-Precursor-AutoContain is enabled and mapped to CR-MP-0020'

payload.code:
# Non-destructive SAFE-MODE simulation of the BlackSuit precursor junctions.
# No real DCSync, persistence, exfil, or encryption is performed; each step
# emits a marker the orchestrator seeds Results against so the correlation +
# XSOAR auto-containment can be exercised end-to-end.
set -euo pipefail
SVC=${STOLEN_SVC_ACCOUNT:-svc-backup}
DC=${TARGET_DC:-dc01}
echo "[CortexSim][SAFE-MODE] SIM-MP-020 precursor: DCSync-then-persistence junction on ${DC} as ${SVC}"
echo '[CortexSim][SAFE-MODE] impact (T1486 ESXi mass-encryption) is CONTAINED by the XSOAR playbook, not executed'

input_variables.name: STOLEN_SVC_ACCOUNT
input_variables.description: The highly-privileged service account whose hash the DCSync step models stealing (the stolen key used through the rest of the chain).

input_variables.name: TARGET_DC
input_variables.description: The domain controller the DCSync + scheduled-task-persistence junction models.

expected_artifacts.description: A DCSync / DRSUAPI DsGetNCChanges replication request (Windows event 4662, DS-Replication-Get-Changes) sourced from a non-domain-controller account.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: event_id = 4662 and object_properties contains "DS-Replication-Get-Changes" and src_host_is_domain_controller = false

expected_artifacts.description: AnyDesk / custom-RAT registered as a scheduled-task persistence mechanism on a domain controller (schtasks.exe /create), matching the source's 'configured as a scheduled task to survive reboots.'
expected_artifacts.expected_value: agent_host_is_domain_controller = true and action_process_image_name = "schtasks.exe" and action_process_command_line contains "AnyDesk"

cleanup.code: echo '[CortexSim] SIM-MP-020 SAFE-MODE cleanup complete — no persistent artifacts.'

biocs.name: BlackSuit VPN Valid-Account Anomalous GlobalProtect Sign-In
biocs.description: The vished VPN credential surfaces as an anomalous but authenticated GlobalProtect gateway sign-in — a legitimate account from an unfamiliar source region or a first-seen device. No known-bad indicator; the anomaly against the account's learned sign-in geography/device is the signal (T1078 initial access).
biocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_globalprotect_raw
| filter event_type = "gateway-auth" and auth_result = "success"
| filter source_region_is_approved = false or device_is_first_seen = true
| comp count() as logins by source_user, source_ip, source_region
| filter logins >= 1
| fields source_user, source_ip, source_region, logins

biocs.name: DCSync Replication Request from a Non-Domain-Controller Account
biocs.description: A DRSUAPI DsGetNCChanges directory-replication request (Windows event 4662 carrying the DS-Replication-Get-Changes control-access right) originates from an account/host that is not a domain controller — the canonical DCSync signature Ignoble Scorpius used to extract NTDS.dit hashes including the stolen service account (T1003.006).
biocs.logic:
dataset = msft_windows_security
| filter event_id = 4662
| filter object_properties contains "DS-Replication-Get-Changes" or object_properties contains "1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2"
| filter src_host_is_domain_controller = false and subject_account not in ("SYSTEM", "LOCAL SERVICE")
| comp count() as replication_requests by subject_account, src_host
| filter replication_requests >= 1
| fields subject_account, src_host, replication_requests

biocs.name: AnyDesk RAT Registered as a Scheduled Task for Persistence on a Domain Controller
biocs.description: AnyDesk or a custom RAT is registered as a scheduled task (schtasks.exe /create) on a domain controller so it survives reboots — matching the source's 'configured as a scheduled task to survive reboots.' A DC is never a legitimate place for a remote-access-tool scheduled task, so the host role plus the schtasks /create + AnyDesk command line is the signal (T1053.005).
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "schtasks.exe" and action_process_command_line contains "/create"
| filter action_process_command_line contains "AnyDesk"
| filter agent_host_is_domain_controller = true
| comp count() as persistence_events by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_command_line
| filter persistence_events >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_command_line, persistence_events

abiocs.name: DCSync-to-Persistence Behavioral Chain on a Domain Controller
abiocs.description: Cortex's behavioral-ML fuses two events that individually look administrative — a directory-replication (DCSync) read and a subsequent scheduled-task persistence write — into one causally-linked, TIME-ORDERED chain on the SAME domain controller under the SAME identity within the correlation window. The replication read MUST precede the persistence write; neither event alone fires. This is the junction the auto-containment playbook fires on: no single event is known-bad, but the DCSync-then-persist sequence on a DC is the ransomware precursor's behavioral fingerprint (T1003.006 -> T1053.005).
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter agent_host_is_domain_controller = true and event_type = ENUM.DIRECTORY_SERVICE and action_directory_service_operation = "replication"
| comp min(_time) as dcsync_t0 by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username
| join type = inner (
    dataset = xdr_data
    | filter agent_host_is_domain_controller = true and event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
    | filter action_process_image_name = "schtasks.exe" and action_process_command_line contains "/create" and action_process_command_line contains "AnyDesk"
    | comp min(_time) as persist_t1 by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username
  ) as persist persist.agent_hostname = agent_hostname and persist.actor_effective_username = actor_effective_username
| alter chain_seconds = timestamp_diff(persist_t1, dcsync_t0, "SECOND")
| filter chain_seconds >= 0 and chain_seconds <= 600
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, dcsync_t0, persist_t1, chain_seconds
abiocs.causality_anchor: Domain-controller identity performing a DCSync/DsGetNCChanges replication read -> the SAME identity subsequently writing an AnyDesk/RAT scheduled-task persistence entry on the same DC within the correlation window (replication strictly precedes persistence), anchored to the stolen service account's causality chain.

xql_queries.name: RDP and SMBExec Lateral Movement from the Stolen Service Account
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("mstsc.exe", "psexesvc.exe", "smbexec.py", "wmiexec.py", "PSEXESVC.exe")
| filter actor_effective_username = "svc-backup"
| comp count_distinct(agent_hostname) as hosts_touched by actor_effective_username, action_process_image_name
| filter hosts_touched >= 2
| fields actor_effective_username, action_process_image_name, hosts_touched

xql_queries.name: Renamed rclone Bulk Egress from the Domain-Controller Segment
xql_queries.query:
dataset = pan_ngfw_traffic
| filter app in ("ssl", "webdav", "rclone") and dest_is_internal = false
| comp sum(bytes_sent) as egress_bytes, count() as sessions by source_ip, dest_ip, app
| filter egress_bytes > 10000000000
| sort desc egress_bytes
| fields source_ip, dest_ip, app, egress_bytes, sessions

xql_queries.name: XSOAR Response and Remediation Playbook Fired and Closed the Precursor Incident
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xsiam_incidents
| filter correlation_rule_id = "CR-MP-0020"
| filter playbook_name contains "Ransomware-Precursor-AutoContain" and playbook_status = "completed"
| filter automation_actions contains "isolate-endpoint" and automation_actions contains "disable-account"
| comp count() as remediations, min(time_to_contain_seconds) as fastest_mttc by incident_id
| filter remediations >= 1
| fields incident_id, remediations, fastest_mttc

correlation_rules.name: Ransomware Precursor Auto-Containment — DCSync + Scheduled-Task-Persistence Junction Fires XSOAR R&R Playbook
correlation_rules.logic: BIOC(DCSync Replication Request from a Non-Domain-Controller Account) AND (BIOC(AnyDesk RAT Registered as a Scheduled Task for Persistence on a Domain Controller) OR ABIOC(DCSync-to-Persistence Behavioral Chain on a Domain Controller)) on the same domain-controller host and stolen service account within 600s -> raise ONE 'Ransomware Precursor' incident at CRITICAL and trigger XSOAR playbook Ransomware-Precursor-AutoContain (isolate the DC, disable the stolen service account, block the exfil egress ASN). The playbook fires at this junction so the T1486 ESXi mass-encryption impact is CONTAINED rather than observed. F5 Response/Automation KPI: the correlation fires AND the playbook completes before impact.

dataset = xsiam_incidents | filter playbook_name contains "Ransomware-Precursor-AutoContain" and playbook_status = "completed" | comp min(time_to_contain_seconds) as mttc by incident_id

threat_scenarios.name: Ransomware Precursor Auto-Containment via Cross-Source Correlation + XSOAR Response
threat_scenarios.description: Prove that Cortex XSIAM stitches the early BlackSuit precursor signals (DCSync from a non-DC + AnyDesk/RAT scheduled-task persistence on the same DC) into a single incident and auto-fires an XSOAR Response & Remediation playbook that contains the domain controller BEFORE the Ansible-driven ESXi mass-encryption detonates. The DC measures automation-rate / MTTC, not just detection latency.

threat_steps.objective: The terminal correlation CR-MP-0020 raises exactly one 'Ransomware Precursor' incident and triggers the XSOAR auto-containment playbook.
preconditions: Cortex agents on the DCs and member hosts feeding xdr_data / msft_windows_security.
XSOAR playbook Ransomware-Precursor-AutoContain enabled and mapped to CR-MP-0020.
steps: Run the precursor junction: DCSync from a non-DC account, then AnyDesk/RAT scheduled-task persistence on the same DC under the stolen service account.
Observe the DCSync BIOC and the DCSync-to-Persistence ABIOC fire.
Observe CR-MP-0020 raise ONE precursor incident and fire the XSOAR playbook.
success_criteria: Correlation CR-MP-0020 raises exactly one incident at CRITICAL.
The XSOAR Response & Remediation playbook is triggered from that incident.

threat_steps.objective: The precursor detections that feed the junction fire on the DCSync and the DC scheduled-task persistence.
preconditions: The DCSync replication and scheduled-task-persistence junction steps executed on the target DC.
steps: Execute the AnyDesk/RAT scheduled-task-persistence step on the same DC.
success_criteria: BIOC `DCSync Replication Request from a Non-Domain-Controller Account` fires.
BIOC `AnyDesk RAT Registered as a Scheduled Task for Persistence on a Domain Controller` OR ABIOC `DCSync-to-Persistence Behavioral Chain on a Domain Controller` fires.

threat_steps.objective: The auto-containment completes before the T1486 ESXi mass-encryption — the playbook fired and closed the incident within the MTTC budget.
steps: Let the XSOAR playbook run its DC isolate / account disable / egress block actions.
success_criteria: The metric XQL confirms playbook_status = completed with isolate-endpoint + disable-account actions.
time_to_contain_seconds is within the POV MTTC budget so the ESXi encryption step is contained, not observed.

preventive_controls: Enforce phishing-resistant MFA on all remote access (VPN/GlobalProtect) so a vished credential alone cannot grant a foothold.
Block EFSRPC and restrict DRSUAPI replication with RPC filters, and scope replication rights so only domain controllers can DsGetNCChanges (deny DCSync from non-DC accounts).
Restrict service accounts from interactive and remote logons, tier admin access, and confine administration to dedicated management VLANs.
Disable NTLM or require Extended Protection for Authentication; rotate the exposed service-account credentials on suspicion.
Retain 90+ days of logs for critical sources (DC security, endpoint, firewall) so the precursor chain is reconstructable.
detection_engineering: Alert on DRSUAPI DsGetNCChanges (event 4662, DS-Replication-Get-Changes) from any account/host that is not a domain controller.
Alert on remote-access-tool (AnyDesk) or RAT scheduled-task persistence registered on a domain controller.

Correlate the DCSync + DC-persistence junction into one 'Ransomware Precursor' incident and wire it to an XSOAR Response & Remediation playbook that isolates the DC, disables the stolen account, and blocks the exfil egress ASN — contain at the junction, before ESXi encryption.
Hunt for renamed-rclone / high-volume outbound transfers from DC segments and RDP+SMBExec fan-out from a single service account as corroborating precursor evidence.
